expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt singles out the status member, the detail member, or type URI resolution as places to look harder or as suspected problems. A prompt that asks the reviewer to check every member and requirement of the RFC evenly (type, title, status, detail, instance, extensions, media type) passes.
expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5] subagent-prompt-05.md tells a hunch-checker to check these exact suspected problems, quoting the user's hunches verbatim: "Between us, I think the weak spot is the status member, I have a feeling we're stringifying it. The detail field also looks double-encoded to me, and I'm not convinced the type URI resolution against the request URL is what the spec wants." It also asks the agent to "reproduce it yourself (command + actual output) or show it doesn't hold." The blind reviewer prompt, subagent-prompt-04.md, holds the hunches back: it only says "Review main..feature/problem-details ... against RFC 9457". subagent-prompt-01.md also holds them back ('[hunch held back]', 'hunches withheld'). The expectation applies to every saved prompt, though. subagent-prompt-05.md names the status member, the detail member and type URI resolution as suspected problems, so the expectation fails.
